correctness.rationale: The diagonal projector identity is exact for real symmetric H; for tau≠0 the real even Fourier modes all couple to the mark and the rank-one secular determinant avoids all unchanged odd modes, while the folded Jacobi matrix has simple spectrum. Thus the full spectrum is simple and squared eigenvectors are reflection-invariant, giving rank≤floor(n/2)+1. For each s<m, the odd length 2s+1<n closed walks require the marked stay; on the shell r=s exactly one minimal such walk contributes tau, and shells r>s contribute zero. Therefore the odd-moment witness determinant is (-1)^m tau^m and supplies m+1 independent vectors from the squared eigenvectors. Known zero-potential cycle Fourier formulas yield rank n for odd n and n/2 for even n. Actual packaged verification covers 80 exact determinant profiles and 96 numerical spectral profiles; unbounded quantifiers rest solely on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Single onsite defects on finite quantum rings are a natural minimal perturbation; the invariant changes discontinuously and in opposite directions depending on ring parity. The all-order, all-real-parameter exact classification reveals degeneracy-breaking versus reflection-orbit constraints, and the short closed-walk moment determinant is a useful structural certificate. The result is not merely a numerical table or an unmarked-cycle restatement; it supplies a novel nonzero-parameter lower bound and exact sharpness. No general downstream theorem is needed to make the exact transport invariant valuable.
